props.kicker: A decision forge for agent-built software
props.title: Verdict
props.subtitle: Agents declare intent. ==Evidence decides.== Humans approve.

slides.notes: Verdict is a decision forge for software written by AI agents. The tagline is the whole thesis: intent from the agent, evidence decides, humans approve.

props.title: Agents edit faster than anyone can review.

left.label: Today
left.title: Merges are vibes-based
points: Agents ship diffs faster than humans can read
Reviews sample a fraction of what lands
No account of why a change was accepted

right.label: Unaccountable
right.title: Trust without evidence
points: Acceptance is a gut call, not a measurement
No record to audit when something breaks
Rolling back means untangling history by hand

slides.notes: The gap: generation speed has exploded, review capacity has not. Merges happen on vibes and nobody can say afterwards why a change went in.

props.title: Before editing, the agent declares its ==intent==. Candidates compete. Tests decide.
props.body: Candidate implementations face off in a tournament judged by deterministic evaluation and held-out tests. The LLM explains and ranks — ==it never decides.==

slides.notes: Flip review on its head: intent comes first, then a tournament of implementations scored by evidence. The model's job is explanation and ranking — the decision belongs to deterministic evaluation and, finally, the human.

items.title: Declare intent
items.body: The agent states what it will change before touching code

items.title: Fork per agent
items.body: Every candidate implementation gets its own sandbox

items.title: Deterministic eval
items.body: Held-out tests score each candidate the same way

items.title: One decision card
items.body: A single verdict per intent — the LLM explains and ranks, never decides

items.title: Fast-forward-only merge
items.body: A sequencer keeps history linear and replayable

items.title: Ledger + undo
items.body: Append-only decision record with one-click rollback

slides.notes: Walk the pipeline left to right: intent declared up front, candidates forked and scored by the same held-out tests, a single decision card per intent, then a fast-forward-only merge recorded in an append-only ledger with one-click undo.

tiles.title: Workers
tiles.body: Edge runtime orchestrates tournaments and the merge sequencer

tiles.title: Artifacts
tiles.body: Candidate implementations live as immutable build artifacts

tiles.title: D1
tiles.body: The append-only decision ledger — every verdict, permanently queryable

slides.notes: Everything runs on Cloudflare: Workers drive the tournaments and the merge sequencer, Artifacts hold the candidate implementations, and D1 is the append-only ledger.

items.title: The LLM never decides
items.body: It explains and ranks; deterministic evaluation holds the pen

items.title: One decision per intent
items.body: A single verdict card — no silent competing merges

items.title: Append-only ledger
items.body: Every acceptance reason is permanent and auditable

items.title: One-click undo
items.body: Reverse any decision without rewriting history

slides.notes: The four guarantees: the model never holds the pen, one verdict per intent, a ledger that cannot be rewritten, and undo that respects history.
